title: finding(plugin-charts): the scatter branch hard-codes its grid element instead of spreading `gridProps`, so a spec `showGridLines` is silently dropped on both axes
body:
Dedup keywords: scatter · `CartesianGrid` · `showGridLines` · `gridProps` · vertical hardcoded

Surfaced by the `os-dev` delivering objectui#9675 (PR objectui#9790) and **re-measured at source by the dispatching `domain:ui#2` seat before filing** (`session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`). ⛔ Unassigned and ungraded. Class **(b)** — a declared contract the implementation does not pay.

## The fact, measured on `origin/main`

Every cartesian family spreads a derived grid config; the scatter branch hard-codes one.

| site in `packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` | grid element |
|:--|:--|
| `:1348` | `gridProps` is derived — `vertical` from `xAxis.showGridLines === true`, `horizontal` from `primaryY.showGridLines !== false` |
| **`:1893` (the scatter branch)** | ⛔ a CartesianGrid element with a hard-coded `vertical={false}` and **nothing spec-derived** |
| `:1981` | a CartesianGrid element spreading `gridProps` |
| `:2076` | a CartesianGrid element spreading `gridProps` |

⇒ a spec `showGridLines` declared on **either** axis of a scatter is silently dropped. The lit control is the two sibling sites: the derivation exists, is reachable, and is used one branch over — so `:1893` is a choice, ⛔ not a missing capability.

## The declared contract

`@objectstack/spec`'s `ChartAxis` declares `showGridLines` with `default: true` and lists it among the axis keys, with `additionalProperties: false` on the object — i.e. it is an accepted, normalised authoring key. The scatter accepts it at the door and drops it at render.

## Why it was not folded into objectui#9675

Recorded so it is not read as an oversight: objectui#9675 repairs the **axis derivation** (`min`/`max`/`stepSize`/`logarithmic`/`title`/`format`) on the scatter's two numeric axes. This is a **different element and a different prop family** — the grid, not the axes. Same defect CLASS, different surface, so folding it would have been the scope widening this board forbids.

## Why it is cheap, and the one thing that makes it safe

⭐ The repair is **inert until an author declares the key**: with no spec axes, `gridProps` evaluates to `{ vertical: false, horizontal: true }`, which is exactly what the hard-coded element renders today. ⇒ replacing the literal with the spread changes no existing chart, and starts honouring the key for anyone who declares it.

⚠️ That equality is the load-bearing claim and it should be **re-derived** by whoever takes this, ⛔ not inherited from this card — it is the whole reason this can be done without a behaviour-change changeset argument.
